title: Bridging the Bio-Electronic Interface with Biofabrication
protocol: Connect a power supply to the custom fabricated electrodes via patch cords using alligator clips.
Position an ITO-covered glass slide as the anode opposing the platinum foil cathode.
Prepare an alginate deposition solution by mixing 1% alginate and 0.5% CaCO3 in distilled water, then autoclave it.
Submerge both electrodes into the prepared alginate deposition solution.
Apply a constant current density of 3 A/m2 for 2 minutes.
Disconnect the electrode and remove the non-deposited solution.
Gently rinse the film with NaCl (0.145 M).
Incubate the film briefly (~1 min) in CaCl2 (0.1 M).
Rinse the film again with NaCl (0.145 M).
Incubate the film in a desired solution supplemented with CaCl2 (1 mM).
Image the resulting film using a fluorescence microscope.
Reconstitute W3110 wt E. coli culture grown overnight in LB media and re-inoculate for growth to an optical density of 1 at 600 nm.
Reconstitute MDAI2 + pCT6-lsrR-ampr + pET-dsRed-kanr culture grown overnight in LB media with kanamycin and ampicillin, and re-inoculate for growth to an optical density of 1 at 600 nm.
Adjust the optical density of the receiver cell culture to 0.4-0.6 using LB media.
Prepare a deposition solution containing 2% alginate and 1% CaCO3.
Mix each cell culture with the deposition solution in a 1:1 ratio, resulting in a final concentration of 1% alginate, 0.5% CaCO3, and cells diluted to about half the culturing density.
Place a glass slide patterned with two ITO electrodes contained by a PDMS well on a platinum counter electrode.
Connect one ITO electrode to a power supply as described in Procedure 1 (Alginate electrodeposition).
Immerse the connected ITO electrode in the deposition solution containing the receiver cells.
Set the power supply to a constant current density of 3 A/m2, where the surface area dimension is defined by the single electrode on which deposition will occur.
Apply the constant current for 2 minutes to allow for codeposition of the cells in the alginate matrix.
Rinse the film as described in Step 1.5.
Switch the anodic connection from the first ITO electrode to the second, adjacent, ITO electrode.
Repeat the deposition procedure using a solution containing sender cells.
Incubate the 2-electrode chip with codeposited cells and calcium-alginate overnight at 37°C in PBS supplemented with 10% LB media and 1 mM CaCl2.
Image the incubated samples using a fluorescence microscope.
Connect the power supply to the electrodes via alligator clips.
Position the gold-coated silicon chip as the cathode (working electrode) against a platinum foil anode (counter-electrode).
Submerge the desired area for deposition into a chitosan solution (0.8%) completely.
Prepare a chitosan solution by mixing chitosan flakes with water and adding 2 M HCl to achieve a final pH of 5.6.
Label the chitosan solution with 5-(and-6)-carboxyrhodamine 6G succinimidyl ester for fluorescence imaging.
Apply a constant current density of 4 A/m2 for 2 minutes.
Rinse the electrode with DI water to remove superfluous chitosan.
Attach the treated electrode to a three-electrode system as the working electrode, using platinum wire as the counter-electrode and Ag/AgCl as the reference electrode.
Immerse the electrodes into a phosphate buffer solution containing 0.1 M NaCl and pH 7.0.
Apply a constant voltage of 0.9 V for 60 seconds to electrochemically conjugate the protein to the chitosan film using chronoamperometry.
Place the chip in phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 7.0) and wash for 10 minutes on an orbital shaker.
Re-attach to the three-electrode system.
Immerse into a solution of 5 mM glucose.
Sweep the potential in a positive direction to 0.7 V using cyclic voltammetry.
Rinse with phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 7.0).
Place the electrodes into a 10 mL beaker containing 8 mL of phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 7.0).
Bias the GOx-functionalized chip to 0.6 V to serve as the working electrode.
Add aliquots of glucose to the buffer, increasing the concentration by 4 mM each time.
Generate a standard curve between the steady state current and the glucose concentration for the GOx-functionalized chitosan film.
Use a glass slide patterned with an adjacent gold and ITO electrode contained within a PDMS well.
Bias the gold electrode with a cathodic potential to electrodeposit chitosan.
Rinse film briefly in DI water.
Rinse film briefly in PBS by pipette.
Add a solution of 3 μM blue fluorescently labeled "AI-2 Synthase" + 100 U/mL Tyrosinase in PBS.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Rinse the film with PBS.
Apply an anodic potential to the ITO electrode.
Codeposit an alginate deposition solution containing receiver cells.
Rinse the films after codeposition.
Add a solution of 500 μM S-adenosyl homocysteine (SAH) in PBS supplemented with 10% LB media and 1 mM CaCl2 to the rinsed films.
Cover the electrodes to prevent evaporation of the added solution.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Image adjacent electrodes using fluorescence microscopy.
Imposed electrical signals can create localized microenvironments near an electrode surface.
Trigger the self-assembly of polysaccharides such as alginate and chitosan to deposit as a hydrogel film on the electrode surface.
Mix alginate and chitosan solutions to achieve sol-gel transitions at the electrode surface.
Deposit biocompatible films such as alginate and chitosan for functionalization with biological components.
Codeposit unique cell populations at separate addresses using alginate films.
Observe interaction between sender and receiver cells where AI-2 diffuses from senders and is taken up by receivers.
Express dsRed red fluorescent protein upon uptake of AI-2 by receiver cells.
Observe red fluorescence only at the electrode where receiver cells are addressed.
Utilize amine groups present on chitosan for pH responsiveness required for electrodeposition.
Conjugate glucose oxidase (GOx) biosensing enzyme to electrodeposited chitosan films electrochemically.
